findings.namedBuyers: Dirk Bernhardt-Walther (University of Toronto) and Lauren Fink (McMaster University) are named 2027 organizers and suitable first relationship contacts, not verified accommodation buyers. Dirk is also the published 2025 conference contact. Lauren is Chair of the LIVELab Operations Committee; McMaster LIVELab is the 2027 ticket-listing organizer. Oshin Vartanian (University of Toronto) and Steven Brown (McMaster University) are also listed organizers. No individual’s hotel contracting authority is established.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced third edition: Tuesday, April 13, 2027, a one-day conference in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Showpass gives 08:00–18:00 EDT on that date. This is an activity date, not a publication or submission date, and is within the requested horizon. No 2028 edition announcement was located; do not project an April 2028 date.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel profile and published event positioning: a city academic event is more relevant than a resort programme, but fit is weak and lodging demand unqualified. TASC describes a one-day gathering of researchers, scholars and students “from across the Greater Toronto Area and beyond”; the 2026 departmental recap reports only “Dozens,” not an exact count. A 157-room hotel should not underwrite a major block on this evidence. Possible business is individual visiting-speaker/researcher lodging or a small voluntary allocation, only if travel demand is confirmed. The listed 2027 Brooklyn College keynote provides a reason to ask about nonlocal travel, not proof of a booked stay. The hotel’s Harbourfront/MTCC advantage does not put it at the university venue. Do not sell the full conference relocation, a 15–109-room block, receptions or catering without requirements and operational verification.
findings.venueCommitments: Paul Cadario Conference Centre (Croft Chapter House), University College, University of Toronto; 15 King’s College Circle, Toronto, ON M5S 3H7. Toronto proper, University of Toronto St. George campus: downtown university district, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. The event website and ticket page announce this non-hotel venue for 2027. This establishes a published venue selection, not inspection of a signed contract. No incumbent lodging hotel is identified.
findings.historicalRotation: April 8, 2025 and April 14, 2026 editions both list the same Paul Cadario Conference Centre, University College, Toronto. The announced April 13, 2027 edition remains there. Evidence supports three consecutive April editions and campus continuity, not a destination-rotation programme, guaranteed annual recurrence or an announced 2028 cycle.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. No edition-specific host hotel, room block, hotel list, official housing bureau, lodging RFP, peak rooms or room-night figure was located on the reviewed event, ticketing and historical edition pages. Published sourcing-related wording is limited to ticketing: “Registration and payment are handled through Showpass.” That is not a housing appointment. Every hotel listed for this edition: none found. Do not infer hotel sourcing is open or that attendees necessarily self-book.
findings.organizationStructure: Academic, cross-university organizing collaboration involving University of Toronto and McMaster University researchers. The ticket page identifies McMaster LIVELab as organizer; Showpass handles registration/payment. No independent association, corporate scaling-company owner, PCO, DMC or housing agency is identified in the reviewed event sources. Treat the supplied scaling_companies segment as a classification mismatch for review, not as verified organizational structure.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The non-hotel campus venue is already announced, and all three documented editions use it: a practical barrier to capturing the core meeting, not proof of an exclusive contract. No competing lodging commitment, sold-out condition, overflow requirement or unmet room demand was found. Inference: local one-day participation and the campus location constrain overnight conversion; that risk is more material than the hotel’s total capacity. No named hotel competitor is substantiated.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Email Dirk Bernhardt-Walther first and include Lauren Fink in a concise academic-group enquiry. Ask who manages 2027 speaker/delegate accommodation, whether any hotels or university lodging are already arranged, how many travelers require overnight stays, arrival/departure nights, budget and payment responsibility, and whether a hotel referral rate or small allocation is wanted. Offer a room-only proposal only after requirements and hotel availability are checked. Do not hold inventory or promise catering. If no material 2027 need exists, seek permission to reconnect before any later edition is planned; retain as low-priority relationship development rather than qualified demand.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the upcoming 2027 edition, registration is publicly offered, but commercial access to accommodation procurement remains unconfirmed. Venue business should be treated as selected elsewhere; lodging must not be marked committed elsewhere or open because neither is evidenced. There is no published group-housing sales route. Direct organizer enquiry is the supported relationship path.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: modest relationship-development potential for visiting-speaker or researcher lodging in later editions if organizers confirm repeat travel needs. Three same-campus April editions support recurrence evidence, not a 2028 booking opportunity or competitive venue rotation. No evidence supports displacing a hotel incumbent, guaranteed overflow, a destination bid or contracted future room demand.
